sections.label: Chesterton Fence notion
sections.summary: Mr Chesterton lived from 1874 to 1936 and contributed the notion of the Chesterton Fence to public policy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chesterton was born in 1874 and died in 1936, and among his many contributions to public policy was the notion of the Chesterton Fence.

sections.label: Speaker's employment and education
sections.summary: The speaker declares employment at Singapore University of Social Sciences and over 20 years as an educator, and says children leave school well equipped.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Before I progress, I should declare that I am currently employed at Singapore University of Social Sciences and have worked as an educator in one way or another for over 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On many international and domestic metrics, our children leave school with an exceptional education, and well equipped to handle the challenges and excitement of modern life.

sections.label: Including children with disabilities
sections.summary: Children with disabilities or complex behaviours will be safely and respectfully included in mainstream schools alongside their peers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Children with disabilities or with complex and challenging behaviours, will be safely and respectfully included into mainstream schools, to be educated alongside their peers.

sections.label: Multi-disciplinary advisory group
sections.summary: A multi-disciplinary advisory group could be established to research and collate innovative education practice domestically and internationally.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One way to facilitate this would be to establish a multi-disciplinary advisory group, whose task is to research and collate innovative practice within the education sector both domestically and internationally.

sections.label: Partnership, support and progress indicators
sections.summary: Balancing competing demands is achievable through partnership among schools, parents and children, with Government support, and key indicators should monitor progress.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Balancing these competing demands can be difficult but is achievable when schools, parents and children work together in partnership and when the Government does its part to ensure that parents and families are sufficiently resourced and supported to focus on their children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us publicise and promote our agenda for change and put in place key indicators to monitor and assess our progress.

sections.label: Support, responsibility and restoration
sections.summary: Schools should encourage children to take responsibility, provide individualised multi-tiered support for reintegration, and create environments based on restoration and repair rather than coercion and punishment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Schools also need to be places, where children are encouraged and allowed to take responsibility for their actions, including their behaviour, goals and learning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need to provide individualised, multi-tiered systems of support to ensure that all children can be reintegrated back into the school community if and when they start to disengage or fall behind.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need to create cohesive environments that are based on the concept of restoration and repair, not coercion and punishment when harm is done.

sections.label: A-level and G2 subject admission
sections.summary: Students may count a fourth content-based A-level subject for university admission from 2026 and one G2 subject for Polytechnic Year 1 from 2028, if it improves their score.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For example, we are allowing students to count their fourth content-based A-level subject for admission to our Autonomous Universities only if it improves their University Admission Score from 2026 and to count one G2 subject for admission to Polytechnic Year 1 from 2028.

sections.label: Full Subject-based Banding learning
sections.summary: Full Subject-based Banding lets students customise learning in individual subjects instead of keeping one pace across all subjects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For example, Full Subject-based Banding now allows students to customise their learning in individual subjects instead of keeping to one pace across all subjects.

sections.label: MOE support for teachers
sections.summary: MOE is stepping up teachers' personal growth and professional development through educational technology, well-being support, and redesigned staff rooms and workspaces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They pour their hearts out to bring out the best in our children, often going above and beyond the call of duty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is why MOE is stepping up efforts for our teachers' personal growth and professional development by (a) investing in educational technology to support our teachers' pedagogical practices, alleviate their workload and enable them to deliver customised teaching; (b) supporting our teachers' well-being through curated resources, workshops and counselling services; and (c) even redesigning staff rooms and workspaces to better meet their professional needs, as recently announced by the Prime Minister at the National Day Rally.

sections.label: Strengthening industry partnerships
sections.summary: Partnerships, especially with industry, will be strengthened to inspire younger students early and help adult learners keep up with industry changes through co-designed modules.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Member may be pleased to know that we will strengthen these partnerships, especially with the industry: to inspire younger students and shape their interests early and to help our adult learners keep up to date with industry changes by co-designing, co-developing and co-delivering modules with our institutes of higher learning.

sections.label: Avoiding over-structuring education
sections.summary: Even as the education system is enhanced, care must be taken not to over-structure, over-provide or over-protect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Even as we enhance our education system, we must be careful to not over-structure, over-provide or over-protect.

sections.label: MOE commitment and sitting time
sections.summary: MOE is committed to working with all partners to improve education so Singapore and Singaporeans thrive, and tomorrow's Sitting will commence at 11.00 am.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: MOE is committed to work with all partners to improve our education system so that Singapore and Singaporeans can thrive in the years and generations to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 11.00 am.
